text.arabic_uthmani: لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌۭ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌۭ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌۭ ۗ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۖ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ يُعَذِّبْهُ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًۭا

words.gloss_range: frozen defective negator denying the presence of burden in the current legal state
words.root_gloss_range: negation of being or attribution; here it denies the existence of legal burden rather than narrating an action
words.prose: {{ar:لَيْسَ}} ({{tr:laysa}}), from {{ar:ل ي س}} ({{tr:l-y-s}}), opens by denying that burden exists in the relevant legal state. Its frozen defective form and fronted burden phrase make the first sound a removal of liability, and the repeated formula known from 24:61 and 9:91 is specialized here by the prior martial summons.

topics.headline: negated liability opens the exemption frame
topics.summary: The reader notices that the ayah first removes a legal state of liability before naming the exempted bodies.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah first removes a legal state of liability before naming the exempted bodies.
topics.reason: The rows cohere around an uninflected negator, fronted predicate structure, repeated no-burden formula, and a boundary shift from summons to exemption.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the bearer on whom liability would rest before negation removes it
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) supplies the burden-bearing slot: liability is imagined as something resting upon someone. Under the opening negation, that imposed weight is what gets removed, so the preposition turns spatial pressure into legal incumbency.

topics.headline: burden imagined as placed upon a bearer
topics.summary: The reader notices that the exemption is framed as weight lifted from a bearer, not merely a soft exception.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exemption is framed as weight lifted from a bearer, not merely a soft exception.
topics.reason: The rows fit the QAC account of the preposition governing the exempted person and selecting obligation or liability under negation.

words.gloss_range: definite substantive adjective naming the blind person as an exempt legal category
words.root_gloss_range: physical and metaphorical blocked perception; this bodily exemption list selects physical blindness while leaving the wider register as contrast
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ}} ({{tr:al-aʿmā}}), from {{ar:ع م ي}} ({{tr:ʿ-m-y}}), turns an adjective of blocked perception into a definite substantive class. The broader root can speak of physical or spiritual blindness, but the surrounding bodily triad narrows this occurrence to physical incapacity within a legal exemption also echoed at 24:61.

topics.headline: blindness as a definite exempt class
topics.summary: The reader notices that blindness is not a casual description but a named class from which combat-related burden is lifted.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that blindness is not a casual description but a named class from which combat-related burden is lifted.
topics.reason: The row family survives as a class-and-root payoff, narrowed by the disability triad and the prepositional burden frame.

words.gloss_range: indefinite no-burden noun denying any relevant constriction, blame, or liability
words.root_gloss_range: narrowness, constriction, and moral blame; here the legal formula removes constricting liability from incapacity
words.prose: {{ar:حَرَجٌ}} ({{tr:ḥarajun}}), from {{ar:ح ر ج}} ({{tr:ḥ-r-j}}), lands as an indefinite delayed subject: any relevant constriction, blame, or liability is denied. Its first occurrence completes the blind-person clause, begins the threefold refrain, and keeps legal relief for incapacity distinct from the later obedience/refusal accountability.

topics.headline: indefinite constriction and blame removed
topics.summary: The reader notices that the first exemption removes both practical constriction and blame, not just one named duty.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first exemption removes both practical constriction and blame, not just one named duty.
topics.reason: The rows converge on indefiniteness, delayed subject syntax, constriction/blame semantics, threefold refrain, and formulaic echoes such as 9:91 and 24:61.

words.gloss_range: conjunction extending the same negative exemption frame to the next category
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) carries the exemption forward to a second category while preserving the original no-burden frame. Its force is additive and dependent: the legal rule stays the same even as the listed body condition changes.

topics.headline: coordination keeps the second class inside negation
topics.summary: The reader notices that the second exempt category is added under the same rule rather than introduced as a separate ruling.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second exempt category is added under the same rule rather than introduced as a separate ruling.
topics.reason: The rows identify coordination with the following negator as a wa-la unit that extends the prior negated liability frame.

words.gloss_range: negative particle continuing the opening negation into the second exemption phrase
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) keeps the original negation active in the second exemption. It does not restart the syntax as a fresh denial; joined to the preceding conjunction, it lets the same legal release cover the next burden-bearing phrase.

topics.headline: inherited negation without restating the verb
topics.summary: The reader notices that the second phrase inherits the full legal negation without needing the opening verb again.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second phrase inherits the full legal negation without needing the opening verb again.
topics.reason: The rows support a carried negation reading rather than an independent new predicate.

words.gloss_range: repeated burden-governing preposition placing the second class in the same legal slot
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) repeats the same burden-bearing slot for the second category. The repeated preposition makes the exemption parallel and non-hierarchical: the imagined legal weight is placed in the same position so it can be lifted in the same way.

topics.headline: parallel liability slot for the lame
topics.summary: The reader notices that the lame category occupies the same burden-bearing grammar as the blind category.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lame category occupies the same burden-bearing grammar as the blind category.
topics.reason: The rows converge on repeated prepositional government and the concrete-to-legal burden image.

words.gloss_range: definite substantive adjective naming mobility impairment as an exempt category
words.root_gloss_range: limping, crooked motion, and ascent; the local exemption selects impaired earthly movement while the broader ascent field remains a contrast
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَعْرَجِ}} ({{tr:al-aʿraji}}), from {{ar:ع ر ج}} ({{tr:ʿ-r-j}}), is a definite adjective functioning as a noun for a mobility-impaired class. The root range includes crooked motion and ascent, but this legal list narrows the payoff to restricted bodily movement that cannot bear the prior combat summons in the same way.

topics.headline: lame person as definite mobility-exemption class
topics.summary: The reader notices that restricted movement is made a coequal legal category, with the root image of non-straight motion sharpening the exemption.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that restricted movement is made a coequal legal category, with the root image of non-straight motion sharpening the exemption.
topics.reason: The rows are preserved as a mobility-class payoff, narrowed by the local disability list and burden-governed case relation.

words.gloss_range: repeated indefinite no-burden noun giving the second class its own full release
words.root_gloss_range: narrowness, constriction, and moral blame; here repeated to remove constriction from limited movement
words.prose: {{ar:حَرَجٌ}} ({{tr:ḥarajun}}), from {{ar:ح ر ج}} ({{tr:ḥ-r-j}}), repeats the indefinite no-burden closure for the mobility-impaired class. The repetition matters: constrained movement is not merely appended to the first exemption but receives its own full denial of constriction and blame.

topics.headline: second audible no-burden closure
topics.summary: The reader notices that the second category receives its own audible release from burden instead of relying silently on the first clause.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second category receives its own audible release from burden instead of relying silently on the first clause.
topics.reason: The rows support inherited negation, repeated tanwin force, and parity created by repeating the same legal noun.

words.gloss_range: second coordinating conjunction adding the third exempt category under the same rule
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) extends the exemption sequence to a third category without changing the rule. Its repeated connector role keeps the list formally even, preparing sickness to receive the same no-burden grammar.

topics.headline: coordination extends the triad to sickness
topics.summary: The reader notices that sickness enters as a coequal third category, not as an afterthought.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sickness enters as a coequal third category, not as an afterthought.
topics.reason: The rows identify the conjunction as list-extension inside the repeated wa-la negative connector.

words.gloss_range: negative particle preserving inherited no-burden scope for the third category
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) maintains the inherited negation into the final exemption phrase. The repeated negative particle keeps the syntax as one coordinated no-burden series, so the third category is protected by the same legal force.

topics.headline: negation maintained into the final exemption
topics.summary: The reader notices that no positive obligation re-enters before the sick category is named.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no positive obligation re-enters before the sick category is named.
topics.reason: The rows show that the particle continues the original laysa-negation through a repeated wa-la form.

words.gloss_range: third burden-governing preposition completing the equalized liability frame
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) completes the triple burden-bearing frame. By repeating the same preposition before the sick category, the verse gives all three bodily limitations the same grammatical position under the removed liability.

topics.headline: third identical burden slot
topics.summary: The reader notices that illness is placed under the same imagined legal weight before that weight is lifted.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that illness is placed under the same imagined legal weight before that weight is lifted.
topics.reason: The rows converge on repeated government, burden imagery, and equalization across the three exemption phrases.

words.gloss_range: definite qualitative noun naming the sick person as the third exempt class
words.root_gloss_range: bodily illness and heart-sickness or unsoundness; this triad selects physical illness while contrasting volitional disease elsewhere
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَرِيضِ}} ({{tr:al-marīḍi}}), from {{ar:م ر ض}} ({{tr:m-r-ḍ}}), names sickness as a definite condition class under the same burden frame. The root can describe bodily illness or heart-sickness, but here the blindness-lameness-sickness triad narrows it to physical unsoundness, making the later painful punishment fall on volitional turning rather than illness itself.

topics.headline: sickness as physical exemption class
topics.summary: The reader notices that physical illness is exempted from burden, while later punishment is reserved for chosen refusal rather than incapacity.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that physical illness is exempted from burden, while later punishment is reserved for chosen refusal rather than incapacity.
topics.reason: The rows preserve the condition-class payoff while narrowing the root range to physical illness in the disability triad; 2:10 remains a contrast for heart-sickness, not the local sense.

words.gloss_range: final repeated indefinite no-burden noun completing the exemption triad
words.root_gloss_range: narrowness, constriction, and moral blame; here the third repetition completes legal relief before accountability resumes
words.prose: {{ar:حَرَجٌ}} ({{tr:ḥarajun}}), from {{ar:ح ر ج}} ({{tr:ḥ-r-j}}), gives sickness its own complete no-burden predicate and closes the threefold refrain. Because the previous summons supplies the obligation-domain, this final repetition marks the limit of combat burden before the ayah turns to whoever obeys or turns away.

topics.headline: third no-burden close before the pivot
topics.summary: The reader notices that the exemption triad is syntactically complete before the ayah pivots to universal accountability.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exemption triad is syntactically complete before the ayah pivots to universal accountability.
topics.reason: The rows converge on inherited negation, the third tanwin closure, the completed triad, and the boundary from martial obligation to exempt bodies.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction launching the conditional half rather than adding another exempt class
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge after the completed exemption refrain. It resumes discourse rather than adding a fourth class, shifting the ayah from bodily limits to the universal obedience/refusal structure that still applies after legal burden is lifted.

topics.headline: hinge from exemption to accountability
topics.summary: The reader notices that bodily exemption does not become moral exit; the ayah pivots from released burden to universal consequence.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that bodily exemption does not become moral exit; the ayah pivots from released burden to universal consequence.
topics.reason: The rows identify this conjunction as istiʾnaf/resumption, a rhythm break after three no-burden landings, and the boundary into the conditional binary.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle making obedience a universal condition rather than a named-group report
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the first universal condition after the exemption list. Its payoff is scope: the ayah moves from named bodily categories to an open whoever, so release from combat burden does not remove anyone from the obedience/refusal architecture.

topics.headline: open whoever subject after exemptions
topics.summary: The reader notices that the subject expands to whoever, including but exceeding the exempted classes.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the subject expands to whoever, including but exceeding the exempted classes.
topics.reason: The rows converge on conditional function, open reference, matched man-branches, and the boundary shift from second-person warning in 48:16 to universal condition.

words.gloss_range: Form IV jussive obedience verb governing two coordinated objects under one condition
words.root_gloss_range: willingness and compliance; here Form IV directs active compliance toward named authority rather than bare willingness
words.prose: {{ar:يُطِعِ}} ({{tr:yuṭiʿi}}), from {{ar:ط و ع}} ({{tr:ṭ-w-ʿ}}), makes willingness into directed obedience: one jussive Form IV verb governs the two objects that follow. The local sense is not passive willingness in general but active compliance, and the boundary from 48:16 makes the earlier obedience demand explicit.

topics.headline: volitional obedience to named authority
topics.summary: The reader notices that obedience is a chosen alignment directed to two explicit objects under a single conditional verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that obedience is a chosen alignment directed to two explicit objects under a single conditional verb.
topics.reason: The rows preserve root willingness, Form IV transitivity, jussive conditional mood, two-object governance, and parallels such as 4:13, narrowed to local obedience rather than broad willingness.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in direct-object position as the first explicit obedience target
words.root_gloss_range: worship/deity derivation with noted alternative pressures; here the proper name fixes the determinate divine referent
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}), from {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}), stands as the determinate accusative object of obedience. Derivational debates remain background, but the local grammar narrows the payoff to the named divine referent that governs the paired messenger object under one obedience act.

topics.headline: determinate divine object of obedience
topics.summary: The reader notices that obedience is anchored first in the named divine object, not in an abstract or generic authority.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that obedience is anchored first in the named divine object, not in an abstract or generic authority.
topics.reason: The rows support proper-name definiteness, direct-object syntax, divine-messenger pairing, and local narrowing of broader derivational pressure.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining the messenger to the divine object under the same verb
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the second obedience object to the first under one verb. The conjunction makes the pair syntactically compact: there is one conditional act of obedience, not two disconnected predicates.

topics.headline: one verb binds two obedience objects
topics.summary: The reader notices that the messenger is not a separate clause but the second object of the same obedience act.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the messenger is not a separate clause but the second object of the same obedience act.
topics.reason: The rows converge on object coordination, waṣl, and prevention of a separate-clause reading.

words.gloss_range: singular possessed messenger noun as the second direct object of obedience
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatch, and release; here messenger authority is the sent channel possessed by the divine referent
words.prose: {{ar:رَسُولَهُ}} ({{tr:rasūlahu}}), from {{ar:ر س ل}} ({{tr:r-s-l}}), completes the paired object field of obedience. The suffix makes the messenger definite by relation to God, and the sending-root payoff keeps his authority grounded in delegated dispatch before the reward clause begins.

topics.headline: possessed messenger completes the condition
topics.summary: The reader notices that the messenger is grammatically inseparable from the obedience condition and defined by divine possession.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the messenger is grammatically inseparable from the obedience condition and defined by divine possession.
topics.reason: The rows cohere around second-object syntax, possessed definiteness, sent-channel semantics, same-surah messenger thread, and specification of the prior ayah’s obedience object.

words.gloss_range: Form IV jussive apodosis causing the obedient subject to enter the reward domain
words.root_gloss_range: entering and boundary crossing; here Form IV selects caused admission by an unstated divine agent
words.prose: {{ar:يُدْخِلْهُ}} ({{tr:yudkhilhu}}), from {{ar:د خ ل}} ({{tr:d-kh-l}}), answers the obedience condition with caused admission. The suffix routes the reward to the conditional subject, the Form IV makes entry externally granted, and the yā/nūn reading variation preserves the same reward-punishment balance while shifting discourse voice.

topics.headline: caused entry as reward apodosis
topics.summary: The reader notices that reward is not self-entry but caused admission of the obedient subject across a boundary into gardens.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reward is not self-entry but caused admission of the obedient subject across a boundary into gardens.
topics.reason: The rows preserve jussive apodosis, object suffix, Form IV causation, garden-admission formula echoes at 4:13 and 48:5, and canonical variant balance, narrowed to caused reward entry.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural gardens as the admitted domain, described by flowing rivers
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealment, gardens, hidden beings, and shieldedness; here the garden sense carries protected covered abundance
words.prose: {{ar:جَنَّٰتٍ}} ({{tr:jannātin}}), from {{ar:ج ن ن}} ({{tr:j-n-n}}), names the domain into which the obedient subject is admitted. The broad concealment family narrows here to gardens, while the indefinite plural and following flow-description make the reward feel multiple, sheltered, and internally abundant, echoing the reward scene at 48:5.

topics.headline: covered plural gardens as reward domain
topics.summary: The reader notices that the reward is a plural covered domain of abundance, not a flat single destination.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reward is a plural covered domain of abundance, not a flat single destination.
topics.reason: The rows converge on governed destination/object status, descriptive attachment, concealment-to-garden semantics, plural indefiniteness, stable garden-flow formula, and same-surah reward echo.

words.gloss_range: imperfect intransitive flow verb describing the gardens through their running rivers
words.root_gloss_range: running, flowing, and course-motion; here selected for continuous watercourse movement inside the reward scene
words.prose: {{ar:تَجْرِي}} ({{tr:tajrī}}), from {{ar:ج ر ي}} ({{tr:j-r-y}}), turns the reward noun into a moving scene. The imperfect form gives ongoing flow, the simple Form I keeps the river movement natural, and the verb-before-subject order lets flow be heard before the rivers themselves are named.

topics.headline: ongoing flow animates the gardens
topics.summary: The reader notices that the gardens are animated by ongoing channel-flow rather than presented as static space.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the gardens are animated by ongoing channel-flow rather than presented as static space.
topics.reason: The rows support ongoing imperfect flow, watercourse selection, nonhuman plural agreement, descriptive clause order, and same-surah reward cadence.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking emergence from beneath rather than mere location near the gardens
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) marks the source of the flow. Before the beneath-phrase, it does more than locate rivers near the gardens; it makes abundance emerge from within the reward domain’s lower space.

topics.headline: source of the river flow
topics.summary: The reader notices that the rivers are sourced from beneath the gardens, giving the reward scene internal depth.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rivers are sourced from beneath the gardens, giving the reward scene internal depth.
topics.reason: The rows converge on source relation, emergence from below, and the boundary inversion from exposed summons to sheltered under-garden flow.

words.gloss_range: locative complement with feminine suffix, making beneathness belong to the gardens
words.root_gloss_range: below, beneath, lower place, and possible subordination; here concrete spatial underside is selected
words.prose: {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}), from {{ar:ت ح ت}} ({{tr:t-ḥ-t}}), gives the reward scene vertical depth. The local river-flow setting selects concrete beneathness rather than abstract subordination, and the suffix ties that underside to the garden domain itself, with same-surah links at 48:5 and 48:18.

topics.headline: garden underside as source-space
topics.summary: The reader notices that the reward scene has vertical depth: the flow comes from the gardens’ own underside.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reward scene has vertical depth: the flow comes from the gardens’ own underside.
topics.reason: The rows preserve governed locative complement syntax, suffix reference to gardens, concrete below-sense, and same-surah under/beneath echoes, narrowed away from abstract subordination.

words.gloss_range: definite broken plural rivers as the subject of flow and recognizable reward-formula element
words.root_gloss_range: river, abundant watercourse, daylight, and rebuke; here watercourse abundance is selected
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:al-anhāru}}), from {{ar:ن ه ر}} ({{tr:n-h-r}}), names the flowing subject that completes the garden formula. The broader root includes daylight and rebuke fields, but the local verb selects abundant watercourse; the definite broken plural makes the rivers a familiar manifold element of the reward idiom.

topics.headline: familiar plural rivers complete the reward formula
topics.summary: The reader notices that the reward image resolves into a familiar network of flowing channels, not just generic pleasant scenery.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reward image resolves into a familiar network of flowing channels, not just generic pleasant scenery.
topics.reason: The rows converge on nominative subject status, river-sense selection, broken plural plurality, definiteness, and stable garden-flow collocation.

words.gloss_range: conjunction pairing the refusal condition with the obedience condition
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second conditional branch with the first. Its contrastive effect places whoever turns away beside whoever obeys, so reward and punishment are processed as a balanced binary inside one conditional architecture.

topics.headline: coordination opens the opposite branch
topics.summary: The reader notices that punishment is presented as the matched opposite branch, not an unrelated threat.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is presented as the matched opposite branch, not an unrelated threat.
topics.reason: The rows support coordination of the two man-conditions, contrastive pairing, repeated wa-man launch, and reward/punishment architecture.

words.gloss_range: second conditional particle universalizing culpable turning away
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the refusal condition with the same open scope as the obedience branch. The repeated conditional subject makes the two outcomes formally symmetrical and ensures that no named body class is mistaken for the target of punishment.

topics.headline: open whoever subject for refusal
topics.summary: The reader notices that culpable refusal is universalized to whoever, not limited to a named tribe or disability class.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that culpable refusal is universalized to whoever, not limited to a named tribe or disability class.
topics.reason: The rows converge on second conditional launch, universal scope, repeated man architecture, and boundary expansion from 48:16’s direct warning.

words.gloss_range: Form V jussive turning-away verb without explicit object, triggering the punishment consequence
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, alliance, direction, turning, and protector relations; here refusal is self-directed reorientation away from the named authority
words.prose: {{ar:يَتَوَلَّ}} ({{tr:yatawalla}}), from {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}), makes refusal a self-directed reorientation. The omitted object lets turning away remain open while the prior obedience objects supply the rejected authority, and the same root crossing from 48:16 widens a second-person warning into a whoever-condition.

topics.headline: self-directed reorientation away from obedience
topics.summary: The reader notices that refusal is not mere absence; it is a self-directed shift of allegiance away from obedience.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refusal is not mere absence; it is a self-directed shift of allegiance away from obedience.
topics.reason: The rows preserve object omission, jussive protasis, obedience/refusal antithesis, Form V reflexivity, w-l-y allegiance field, and 48:16 boundary continuity, narrowed to local refusal.

words.gloss_range: Form II jussive apodosis punishing the one who turns away, with object compressed in the suffix
words.root_gloss_range: sweetness/freshness, deprivation, and punishment; here Form II selects imposed punishment while reversing the preceding water-abundance image
words.prose: {{ar:يُعَذِّبْهُ}} ({{tr:yuʿadhdhibhu}}), from {{ar:ع ذ ب}} ({{tr:ʿ-dh-b}}), answers turning away with an intensive caused punishment. The suffix binds the punished patient to the whoever-condition, the sweetness/fresh-water background is narrowed to deprivation and torment, and the verb begins the root-doubled closing formula also continuous with 48:16.

topics.headline: intensive punishment as conditioned consequence
topics.summary: The reader notices that punishment is a matched caused consequence for turning away and it reverses the preceding river-abundance image into deprivation.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is a matched caused consequence for turning away and it reverses the preceding river-abundance image into deprivation.
topics.reason: The rows preserve jussive apodosis, object suffix, Form II intensity, root reversal from sweetness to deprivation, qiraat parallel with the reward verb, 48:16 boundary shift, and cognate-accusative intensification.

words.gloss_range: indefinite cognate accusative naming and intensifying the punishment after the verb
words.root_gloss_range: sweetness/freshness, deprivation, and punishment; here the punishment noun repeats the selected torment branch as an intensifying object
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابًا}} ({{tr:ʿadhāban}}), from {{ar:ع ذ ب}} ({{tr:ʿ-dh-b}}), converts the preceding punishment verb into a cognate noun. The repeated root makes the consequence audible as action and event, while the indefinite accusative leaves its magnitude open for the final pain-quality to specify.

topics.headline: cognate noun doubles the punishment event
topics.summary: The reader notices that the punishment is heard twice: as a verb and then as a named event before the pain adjective closes it.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment is heard twice: as a verb and then as a named event before the pain adjective closes it.
topics.reason: The rows converge on cognate accusative function, masdar form, punishment-event naming, deprivation-image repetition, indefinite magnification, formulaic closure, and continuity with 48:16.

words.gloss_range: accusative indefinite adjective modifying the punishment noun as active pain-producing quality
words.root_gloss_range: pain, ache, and grievousness; here the adjective works actively as pain-causing, not as the sufferer feeling pain
words.prose: {{ar:أَلِيمًا}} ({{tr:alīmā}}), from {{ar:أ ل م}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-m}}), seals the punishment branch by making the punishment itself pain-causing. Agreement ties the adjective to the punishment noun rather than the punished person, and the repeated 48:16 closure frames the contrast between removed burden for incapacity and painful consequence for refusal.

topics.headline: pain-causing adjective seals the ayah
topics.summary: The reader notices that the final word attaches pain to the punishment itself, sealing the ayah with the felt result of culpable turning.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word attaches pain to the punishment itself, sealing the ayah with the felt result of culpable turning.
topics.reason: The rows preserve agreement, active faʿil force, concrete pain-root closure, adjective seal after verb and cognate noun, consecutive-ayah formula, and final sound weight, narrowed away from a passive pain-feeling reading.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three bodily conditions at words 3, 7, and 11 each receive the same negated haraj at words 4, 8, and 12, before the verse resumes with obedience and turning away.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse removes severe constriction and culpability from bodily states while retaining a moral response scaled to actual ability. Because the obedience root also carries capacity, the operative threshold is available responsiveness rather than identical physical performance.

activation_trace.role: Literal loss of sight supplies one concrete limit that cannot fairly be treated as refusal.
Literal lameness supplies impaired locomotion as a second distinct limit on performance.
Weakening and curtailed movement make illness a variable reduction of agency, not a fixed moral type.
Severe narrowness is denied three times, removing a constrictive demand from each body.
The sin-and-scruple image makes the repeated denial an explicit removal of culpability.
Obedient yielding retains moral agency after uniform bodily performance has been waived.
Actual ability supplies the proportional threshold by which obedience can differ across bodies.

changed_reading.before: A list of three compassionate exceptions followed by a generic reward and threat.
changed_reading.after: A differentiated-accountability rule: incapacity cancels constrictive culpability, while whatever responsive agency remains still matters.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse moves from repeated haraj around impaired sight, gait, and health to entry, enclosure, downward space, and flowing rivers.
baseline_models.mechanism: Its two halves form an access topology. Constriction and interrupted movement are cleared; admission then leads into a protected place whose water keeps moving. The reward answers the bodily problem in kind as unobstructed, sustained passage rather than as an unrelated prize.

activation_trace.role: Clustering and entanglement materialize the repeated haraj as crowded blockage.
Bending away from a straight course gives the impaired route a spatial form.
Stopping and lingering supply the temporal interruption that admission reverses.
Literal passage into an interior is the first positive reversal of blockage.
A garden enclosed by growth makes the destination protected without making it confining.
Free running and spreading supply the sustained motion opposite haraj.
Opening and widening until flow is released completes the movement from bottleneck to circulation.

changed_reading.before: Exemption and paradise are adjacent but functionally separate clauses.
changed_reading.after: The paradise clause is a spatial answer to the exemption clause: blocked human routes yield to admitted, protected, continuously flowing life.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse names visible bodily deficits but locates the consequential contrast in obeying versus turning away, followed by entry into a concealed interior.
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus distinguishes what a body visibly cannot do from an inward orientation that can still consent or withdraw. Blindness can activate loss of insight, while entry and garden carry inwardness and concealment; the verse therefore refuses to infer an obscured heart from an impaired body.

activation_trace.role: Blindness of heart supplies the possible moral condition that the literal blind body must not be presumed to possess.
Diminished clarity makes bodily illness a possible but non-identical analogy for obscured inward judgment.
The inner and secret dimension relocates the decisive axis from outward performance to inward orientation.
Covering and concealment make the promised destination continuous with an unseen moral interior.
Turning the face toward something supplies the live orientation presupposed by the negative form.
Withdrawal and turning the back identify culpable refusal as directional, not somatic.

changed_reading.before: The verse contrasts disabled people with able people who obey or disobey.
changed_reading.after: It blocks that social contrast: visible impairment is exempted, while the real contrast runs invisibly through every person as orientation or withdrawal.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Obedience to a messenger leads through admission into ongoing flow, whereas turning away leads to repeated punishment and pain.
baseline_models.mechanism: A chain of willing response, gentle dispatch, entry, and continuous provision forms a circulation. Turning away breaks the sequence; the punishment root's withholding image lets the negative outcome be read as enforced deprivation from that circulation as well as inflicted pain.

activation_trace.role: The self becoming easy for an act initiates circulation through willing availability.
Smooth and easy movement makes messenger-mediated obedience a transmitted path rather than a static command.
Succession and linked portions connect response, admission, and provision into one sequence.
Continuing provision gives the flowing rivers a distributive rather than merely scenic function.
Nearness without an intervening gap names the relation that withdrawal abandons.
Turning away severs the proximity and sequence on which circulation depends.
Restraint, withholding, and weaning render punishment as deprivation from the available flow.
Literal painful punishment prevents the deprivation model from dissolving the verse's explicit threat.

changed_reading.before: Reward and punishment are two externally assigned outcomes.
changed_reading.after: They are also two system states: responsive relation opens sustained circulation, while withdrawal ends in enforced withholding and pain.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening at 48:1 and the first full garden formula at 48:5 turn the focus's access topology into a surah-scale pattern. Opening a closed entrance and releasing water from an outlet recur as admission into a garden with flowing rivers, so the great opening can be measured by whether constricted bodies are given a route rather than forced through one.

activation_trace.role: An opened closure and widened entrance enlarge the focus's denied constriction into the surah's opening mechanism.
Water bursting from its outlet anticipates the released river-flow that answers bodily bottlenecks.
Denied severe narrowness supplies the local closure that opening reverses.
The earlier literal admission establishes that the focus repeats an inclusion formula, not an isolated decorative promise.
The earlier protected garden makes the focus's destination shared with the larger believing body.
The repeated free-running motion confirms flow as a stable answer to constriction.
A river cutting through ground supplies a traversable channel shared by the earlier and focus promises.

structural_cues: The surah opens with a doubled opening root, while the focus repeats haraj three times.
The sequence 'admit - gardens - flow - beneath - rivers' occurs at 48:5 and again at 48:17.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opened entrances, released water, denied narrowness, and an exact reward-formula recurrence; I infer that opening is ethically realized as accessible admission and circulation. A primarily military or political opening remains a live alternative rather than being replaced.

changed_reading.before: The no-haraj rule is a local exception within a chapter about a much larger opening.
changed_reading.after: The local rule discloses the quality of that opening: genuine victory widens entry for constrained bodies and releases shared provision.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context first locates settled and growing faith in hearts, then exposes people who plead busyness while their tongues contradict their hearts and whose bad supposition makes them barren. Against that diagnostic field, the named disabilities are certified constraints: the verse protects real incapacity without ratifying verbal pretext or inward withdrawal.

activation_trace.role: Literal blindness anchors a publicly legible constraint rather than a claimed distraction.
Removal of sin grants genuine incapacity a status that contextually false excuses do not receive.
The literal heart identifies the inward site where responsive capacity is assessed.
Heart-settling security supplies a positive interior state independent of bodily power.
Occupation as the opposite of free availability names the competing excuse offered by the stay-behind speakers.
The speech organ supplies the outward claim that can be detached from inward truth.
Present-state negation explicitly marks what their tongues say as absent from their hearts.
The heart is the concealed comparator against which the excuse fails.
Uncertain supposition supplies the inward mechanism behind outward nonparticipation.
Stagnation until corruption gives failed responsiveness a moral texture unlike bodily impairment.

structural_cues: 48:11 presents wealth and family as claimed causes of staying behind, then explicitly separates tongue from heart.
48:12 supplies the concealed bad expectation behind the claim; 48:17 instead names concrete bodily conditions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a speech-heart discrepancy, corrupting supposition, and then unqualified no-haraj for named conditions; I infer a deliberate boundary between incapacity and pretext. A narrower reading in which 48:17 only lists conventional exemptions, without commenting on excuse-making, remains possible.

changed_reading.before: The exemption simply relaxes an otherwise universal demand.
changed_reading.after: The exemption is also diagnostic protection: it prevents genuine bodily limits from being morally confused with strategic speech, bad expectation, or inward refusal.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pledge scene makes obedience to God and messenger a maintained bond. Its opposite is not mere immobility: breach unravels something previously made firm and harms the breacher, sharpening the focus's turning away into relational disassembly.

activation_trace.role: Mutual accord gives obedience the positive form of maintained alignment.
The messenger and message identify the human relation through which covenantal alignment is enacted.
Turning the back supplies the focus's visible gesture of broken alignment.
A pledge of obedience converts generic compliance into a reciprocal public bond.
Undoing what was firmly tied supplies the material mechanics of turning away.
A preserved covenant supplies the continuity that obedient relation must keep.

structural_cues: 48:10 pairs pledge, breach, self-harm, and fulfillment before the focus pairs obedience, turning, reward, and punishment.
The focus uses a relational verb for refusal rather than a verb of bodily inability.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a pledged relation, its unraveling, and the focus's directional turning; I infer that the threat concerns active covenantal disengagement. Generic obedience without a specific pledge remains a materially live alternative.

changed_reading.before: Turning away means failing to perform the commanded act.
changed_reading.after: Turning away means unraveling a maintained relation; a body unable to perform need not have turned at all.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding ayah summons the stay-behind group to fighting and ends with the same obey/turn/punish sequence. The focus then interrupts that sequence with three no-haraj clauses before restating it. This scopes combat performance by bodily capacity while preserving obedience in forms still available.

activation_trace.role: A verbal summons supplies the concrete demand to which capacity must be assessed.
Reciprocal fighting identifies the high-mobility task from which the named bodies are relieved.
The preceding conditional obedience begins the formula that the focus repeats after inserting exemptions.
Repeated withdrawal marks culpable evasion in the precursor formula.
The identical punishment image locks the two ayat into one conditional frame.
The repeated painful quality confirms deliberate restatement rather than loose thematic resemblance.
Removal of prohibition prevents the combat summons from becoming an indiscriminate rule.
Ability inside obedience permits other available responses after combat performance is waived.

structural_cues: 48:16 and 48:17 share obedience, turning away, punishment, and painful language in the same order.
The only major insertion in the repeated frame is the focus's threefold exemption.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate adjacency, a fighting summons, and near-verbatim conditional repetition; I infer that the insertion calibrates that summons to bodily capacity while leaving a wider field of obedience open. The alternative that every later obedience reference still means participation in the same campaign remains possible but weaker.

changed_reading.before: The disabled are excused from the verse's general moral demand.
changed_reading.after: They are excused from the mobility-intensive combat demand, not removed from moral agency; the repeated conditional resumes on a capacity-sensitive basis.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later context repeatedly limits agency: hands are restrained, an objective lies beyond present capacity yet within divine encompassing, and both sides' hands are restrained under divine sight. The focus's bodily nonperformance can therefore no longer be equated with turning away; stopped action may be incapacity, protection, or providential restraint.

activation_trace.role: Loss of sight anchors involuntary limitation at the level of a particular body.
Curtailed motion supplies a second mode in which non-action is not refusal.
The literal hand makes restrained agency bodily and concrete.
Active prevention shows that an unperformed act can result from imposed restraint rather than disloyalty.
Power sufficient to reach action names capacity as a bounded condition, not a moral constant.
Complete encompassing in knowledge holds what lies beyond current human capacity.
Mutual restraint of hands makes nonviolence itself an enacted outcome.
Divine sight supplies the encompassing witness under which human visual and practical limits are judged.

structural_cues: 48:20 and 48:24 repeat restraint of hands, including the believers' own hands.
48:21 explicitly distinguishes present inability from divine encompassing power.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies bodily restraint, acknowledged inability, encompassing knowledge, and divine sight; I infer that the focus distinguishes three externally similar states: refusal, incapacity, and faithful restraint. The context's restrained hands may instead concern strategy alone, but that does not erase the agency distinction it activates.

changed_reading.before: Obedience appears as action, while turning away appears as non-action.
changed_reading.after: Visible non-action is morally underdetermined: it can be bodily incapacity or protective restraint, so only actual withdrawal warrants the threat.

context_deltas.mechanism: The hidden believers of 48:25 could be trampled because the community cannot distinguish them; force is withheld until bodies can be separated. This activates the focus's named vulnerable bodies as an epistemic-legal brake: commands affecting bodies must account for persons whom collective vision, classification, or power cannot safely handle.

activation_trace.role: Literal blindness anchors limited human perception in the focus's first protected body.
Removal of culpability supplies the legal effect when bodily realities block safe performance.
Knowledge as disclosure marks the missing information that prevents discriminating action.
A foot pressing a place literalizes the risk that collective movement can crush unseen persons.
Severe pressure turns movement into a causal mechanism of unintended bodily harm.
A stain of harm names the liability produced by undifferentiated force.
Separation and distinction supply the absent condition under which targeted punishment could proceed.

structural_cues: 48:25 explicitly says the believing men and women were not known and could have been trampled unknowingly.
Punishment is counterfactually deferred until populations are distinguished; 48:17 likewise distinguishes bodies before restating punishment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies unseen protected persons, trampling, accidental stain, and a separation condition; I infer that the focus's taxonomy performs the same kind of discriminating restraint at the level of capacity. The alternative that 48:25 explains only a particular historical non-engagement remains live.

changed_reading.before: The verse provides individual accommodations for three familiar disabilities.
changed_reading.after: It also models a collective duty of discrimination: power must pause when its categories cannot see or safely carry vulnerable bodies.

context_deltas.mechanism: The movement from heated group pride to tranquility and binding protective speech makes the exemption part of disciplined strength. The repeated no-haraj clauses cool a martial demand before it can become coercive honor: restraint toward limited bodies belongs to obedience, not to its opposite.

activation_trace.role: Serial negation and acquittal give the three clauses the force of a disciplined public limit.
Removing prohibition prevents martial expectation from hardening into coercive law for impaired bodies.
Heated pride and anger supply the affective pressure that could turn participation into an honor test.
Agitated temperament identifies the unstable social force that tranquility must govern.
Cessation of motion cools reactive momentum and makes restraint an active divine gift.
Binding a rule to people supplies disciplined adherence as the alternative to heated compulsion.
Protection from harm gives the binding word a safeguarding function that extends to the exempt.

structural_cues: The focus follows a battle summons but interrupts it with three acquittals.
48:26 opposes heated collective pride with tranquility and a binding word of protection.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies heat, agitated ignorance, tranquility, binding, and protection; I infer that capacity-sensitive exemption is one legal form of cooling collective pressure. The alternative is that 48:26 concerns only the opposing side's disposition and does not directly govern the exemptions.

changed_reading.before: Exemption is compassionate softness beside a chapter of disciplined force.
changed_reading.after: Exemption is itself disciplined force: it restrains honor-driven coercion and binds the community to protection.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing plant does not begin upright and thick: a shoot emerges, supports and is supported, then the plant thickens and stands on its stalk. Read back into the lame and sick bodies, communal strength is developmental and relational; supporting reduced capacity is one way the whole body comes to stand.

activation_trace.role: Impaired legs anchor the changed reading in a body that cannot stand or move conventionally.
Weakening and limited motion supply the vulnerable state that support can carry without condemning.
A shoot emerging beside the original makes growth plural and interdependent from the outset.
Weakness being strengthened directly supplies the support relation carried back to the exempt bodies.
Plants strengthening one another turns support into the causal step before thickness and standing.
A body thickening after thinness makes strength an achieved condition rather than an entry requirement.
Upright completion is the result of the support sequence, not proof of prior self-sufficiency.
The load-bearing stalk and leg create a precise material echo of the focus's impaired leg.

structural_cues: The closing image is explicitly sequential: shoot, mutual strengthening, thickening, uprightness, stalk.
The focus's central bodies are defined by sight, gait, and health rather than by exclusion from the believing collective.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a staged plant mechanism and a branch explicitly naming strengthened weakness; I infer a social analogue in which accommodation contributes to collective uprightness. The plant may alternatively describe communal expansion without any specific disability logic, so the reading remains exploratory.

changed_reading.before: The exemption separates weak members from the community's demanding work.
changed_reading.after: The community's strength may grow through supporting limited members; uprightness is a collective outcome, not a bodily admission test.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the litter and load-bearing branches rather than the ordinary legal sense of haraj. It remains anchored in the repeated haraj, the sick body, and the messenger relation, and downstream prose should present it as a material analogy for obligation, not as a lexical replacement for 'no blame.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The verse repeatedly places haraj upon bodies, while packet branches connect laysa with bearing, haraj with a carrying frame, illness with attendance, and messengerhood with gentleness.

activation_trace.role: Forbearance and carrying whatever is loaded activate obligation as a load borne by a person.
A bier or tightly joined carrying frame gives the otherwise abstract burden a material support structure.
Attending to the sick reverses direction: the limited body is to be supported rather than made to carry.
Gentleness and deliberation qualify how messenger-mediated demands should be carried to constrained people.

changed_reading.before: No legal burden is assigned to the disabled.
changed_reading.after: The command is pictured as a carried load: the rule reverses its direction so that constrained bodies receive support rather than becoming supports for the communal burden.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because the surface 'blind' maps secondarily to an 'amm inventory of generality and collectivity. The packet explicitly supplies that split mapping and the reading remains anchored in the named exception structure; prose should label it a formal activation about general rules, not an etymological claim that 'blind' means 'general.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: A serial negation names three particular bodies before the verse returns to the indefinite 'whoever,' creating tension between particular exceptions and general address.

activation_trace.role: Generality and the collective activate the problem of how a universal command lands on unequal bodies.
Exception that removes the named item supplies the formal operation by which particulars qualify a general field.
The prohibition branch identifies what must not be generalized across bodies without distinction.
Capacity restores a differentiated measure inside the resumed general 'whoever' clause.

changed_reading.before: Three exceptions sit outside a general rule.
changed_reading.after: The exceptions govern how generality itself must work: a collective command becomes just only when particular capacities remain visible inside it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The link is surprising because it turns a repeated preposition into a spatial bridge between pledge and reward. It remains valid through the exact 'under' occurrences, the tree's carrying structure, and returned recompense; prose should call it a compositional echo rather than claim that the tree and gardens are identical symbols.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Rivers flow beneath the gardens in the focus, while the next ayah places the pledge beneath a tree and returns an opening as recompense.

activation_trace.role: Literal beneath-space locates sustaining flow under the promised destination.
A watercourse cutting the ground makes the lower space active and provision-bearing.
The repeated beneath-space places the pledge under a living canopy immediately after the focus.
Interlaced load-bearing wood makes the tree a communal support structure rather than mere scenery.
Recompense returning to the actor connects pledged relation under the tree with the focus's promised return.

changed_reading.before: The exemption leads to a future garden, while the tree pledge is a separate scene of able participants.
changed_reading.after: Two under-spaces coexist: covenant is enacted beneath a supporting canopy, and its sustaining return flows beneath the garden; exemption from one act need not mean exclusion from that relational ecology.

strongest_changes: The near-verbatim 48:16/48:17 frame scopes combat by capacity while preserving other forms of obedience.
The false-excuse and heart sequence prevents genuine bodily incapacity from being read as inward refusal.
Restrained hands and hidden believers make visible non-action morally underdetermined and turn discrimination among bodies into a legal safeguard.
The repeated garden formula recasts the surah's opening as accessible admission and released circulation.
summary.what_was_special: The focus became a hinge between martial summons and protective restraint. Its bodily taxonomy did not shrink the surah's opening; it revealed opening as differentiated access, covenant without coercion, and collective strength capable of carrying unequal bodies.
remaining_uncertainties: The access topology may be a productive compositional echo rather than a governing semantic mechanism.
The epistemic-brake reading depends on carrying 48:25's hidden-body logic back into the exemption list.
The plant-support model is strongly branch-activated but remains a cross-domain social inference.
The load-bearing and split-generality outliers should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Removing entanglement from embodied incapacity.** Repeated `حرج` anchors ح ر ج B001 (dense entanglement), B002 (constriction), and B003 (sin/scruple). Blindness (ع م ي B001), lameness (ع ر ج B001), and illness (م ر ض B001) identify concrete impediments. I infer that exemption untangles legal-moral liability where action is physically constricted. The ayah does more than announce no sin; it clears a knot between inability and blame.
2. **Bodily blindness is not inward blindness.** `الأعمى` directly fits ع م ي B001, while B002 is blindness of heart/insight. The ayah’s explicit exemption, followed by the general obedience condition, prevents automatic transfer from bodily form to inward state. I infer that separating those branches protects moral agency from bodily stigma. Later divine knowledge of hearts (48:18, 48:26) reinforces that correction.
3. **The same destination remains open.** `يطع` retains ط و ع B001/B003; `يدخله` activates د خ ل B001, and the garden/river mechanism repeats 48:5. The exemption precedes, rather than removes, the shared promise. I infer that inability concerning one summons does not bar capable obedience in general. The ayah preserves equal access to the destination while calibrating liability.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 48:18 confirms that hearts, rather than bodily capacity, are the hidden object of knowledge. The exemption therefore clears embodied limitation without lowering inward or communal standing.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Liability untangled from embodied obstruction.** The three fixed repetitions of `حَرَج` anchor ح ر ج `B001`, dense gathering and entanglement, and `B002`, constriction and tightness, alongside legal scruple in `B003`. Ayah 48:16 supplies the severe summons, and 48:22 supplies the nearby counterfactual combat field; the fixed verse inserts blindness, lameness, and illness one by one. The packet supplies duty plus three bodily obstructions; I infer **identified obstruction -> disentanglement of moral liability from non-performance**. Repeated `لَيْسَ ... حَرَج` functions as precise release from a constricted obligation.

2. **Curved gait is not turned allegiance.** Fixed `ٱلْأَعْرَج` anchors ع ر ج `B001` (bodily lameness) and `B002` (curving or turning aside), while fixed `يَتَوَلَّ` anchors و ل ي `B007`, voluntary turning away. The ayah itself places exemption and warning in contrast, after 48:16 used the same withdrawal root for the laggards. I infer **same outward failure to advance + different causal source -> different moral classification**. The verse therefore prevents a bodily deviation from being misread as an inwardly chosen one.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 48:18 supplied a positive case of willing alignment through pledge, known hearts, and returned reward. Ayah 48:22's counterfactual combat then confirmed why the exemption matters: inability to enter a pressure field and choosing to turn one's back in it are not the same mechanism.

baseline.text: Kör için bir sakınca yoktur; topal için bir sakınca yoktur; hasta için de bir sakınca yoktur. Kim Allah'a ve elçisine itaat ederse Allah onu altlarından ırmaklar akan bahçelere koyar. Kim yüz çevirirse ona acı veren bir azap eder.

findings.text: Muafiyet, bedensel engelin daralttığı eylem ile ahlaki sorumluluğu birbirine dolayan düğümü çözer.
Bedensel körlük veya topallık, kalbin körlüğü ya da isteyerek yüz çevirme değildir; aynı dış hareketsizlik farklı nedenlere göre farklı değerlendirilir.
Belirli bir çağrıya katılamamak, kişinin gücü yeten başka itaat biçimleriyle ortak varışa ulaşma imkânını ortadan kaldırmaz.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Bodily limitation is rendered as loss of route, interruption of gait, and constriction of available movement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The exemptions form a navigation scene: blindness removes the track, lameness bends or stops the path, and illness weakens the capacity to continue.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Sight Loss Removes the Track
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Loss of sight expands into loss of insight and then into terrain without a readable route.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: physical blindness (`quranic:root_001049:B001/m01`); blindness of insight (`quranic:root_001049:B002/m01`); trackless land (`quranic:root_001049:B006/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: A bodily limitation becomes a spatial mechanism. What the eye cannot distinguish becomes a landscape without a track, while the insight sense transfers the same obstruction into judgment.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A crooked or weakened gait slows, stops, and narrows the route available to the moving person.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: lameness (`quranic:root_000997:B001/m01`); crooked path (`quranic:root_000997:B002/m01`); stopping or delay (`quranic:root_000997:B003/m01`); illness (`quranic:root_001415:B001/m01`); weakened motion or resolve (`quranic:root_001415:B004/m01`); constriction or strait (`quranic:root_000304:B002/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 48:17 `الأعرج`, `المريض`, and `حرج` (ع ر ج; م ر ض; ح ر ج).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Lameness bends the route and interrupts its traversal; illness reduces the mover's force; constriction names the narrowed field that results. The surface exemptions are thereby reframed as distinct failures in a movement system.
